jobs.title: Pricing Strategy Analyst (Remote)
jobs.jd: We're looking for a Pricing Strategy Analyst to join Procore's Corporate Strategy team. In this role, you'll be the data and analytics engine behind our pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy, turning transaction, sales, and product data into the commercial signals that inform our decisions. You'll also lead smaller pricing initiatives across the full Procore portfolio, including our emerging AI offerings. The primary goal of this role is to make sure Procore's pricing decisions are grounded in clear, accurate, and well-sourced data. As a Pricing Strategy Analyst , you'll partner with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing to analyze how our pricing and packaging perform in the market and to build the visibility needed to improve them. Use your structured problem-solving, data analysis, and executive communication skills to shape how Procore captures value from what we build and buy. If you want hands-on work to drive top line growth and connect everyone in construction, apply today and join our team! This position reports to the Senior Manager of Pricing & Monetization Strategy and can be based remotely in the US. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead pricing and packaging initiatives from hypothesis through recommendation, in partnership with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing Build and stress-test the business case behind pricing decisions, including segment-level performance, cannibalization-adjusted ARR impact, and migration and monetization sizing. Analyze transaction, bookings, discounting, and product data to identify the commercial signals that explain how our pricing and packaging perform, and diagnose the root cause when they underperform, whether it is package design, sales execution, or market fit. Design and run market, competitive, and willingness-to-pay research, including win/loss and price elasticity analysis, to pressure-test pricing hypotheses before they reach leadership. Build and maintain pricing and packaging reporting and dashboards that give Product, Sales, and Finance visibility into performance, working with data teams to keep metrics and data sources accurate and consistent. Translate analysis into a small number of clear, claim-driven recommendations, present them to executive leaders, and defend them under challenge. Partner with Pricing Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, and Marketing to make sure approved decisions are operationalized and communicated to the field. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, strategy, business or data analytics, financial planning and analysis, or consulting wi th 2+ y ears inside a pricing or monetization practice at a top-tier strategy firm Track record of framing ambiguous problems into clear analytical frameworks and presenting recommendations to cross-functional and senior audiences. Experience leading projects or workstreams from analysis through recommendation, with the ability to balance multiple priorities. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, with experience building revenue impact and unit economics models. Hands-on experience querying and analyzing large datasets (e.g., SQL), building reports in a BI tool (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) is a plus Ability to synthesize qualitative inputs, such as call transcripts and field feedback, into clear themes that support pricing recommendations. Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills, with experience partnering with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing teams. Familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics (e.g., ARR, net revenue retention, win rate, discount rate) is a plus Curiosity, high agency, and an owner’s mindset with a strong bias for action. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 81,600.00 - 112,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

ROLE OVERVIEW...

We’re looking for a Data Scientist with 2+ years of experience to turn complex data into models, insights, and recommendations that improve business performance. You’ll tackle problems involving customer behavior, marketing effectiveness, sales conversion, and forecasting, partnering with business stakeholders, data engineers, and machine learning engineers.

This role combines a strong foundation in statistics and machine learning with the ability to apply AI and large language models (LLMs) to practical business problems.



CORE RESPONSIBILITIES...

 - Partner with marketing, sales, and operations teams to define business problems, establish success metrics, and identify opportunities to improve conversion, revenue, and efficiency.

 - Explore and combine data from multiple sources using SQL and Python. Investigate data quality issues, develop features, and document assumptions.

 - Build and evaluate predictive models for use cases such as customer propensity, lifetime value, segmentation, and forecasting.

 - Apply statistical analysis and experimentation to understand performance drivers, measure impact, and communicate uncertainty and limitations.

jobs.jd: Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team. Analytics Engineer We’re hiring Analytics Engineers to join Convene Hospitality Group’s (CHG) Technology organization. We’re building out the foundational platform to democratize data at CHG so that a venue GM, a finance lead, and an AI agent are all able to ask a question and get the same trusted answer. Analytics engineers own the full path from ingestion to visualization, including governance and observability. You’ll bring data in from source systems, model it through bronze, silver, and gold, define the semantic layer, and breathe life into the visualizations, conversational analytics, and business agents that teams rely on to make decisions. You’ll join the Data Platform team, reporting to its Engineering Manager, and work closely with other analytics engineers and business partners across the company. You’ll build on Snowflake, dbt, and Fivetran, using Snowflake-native capabilities like semantic views and Cortex to power ThoughtSpot and beyond. What You’ll Do: Partner with the business. Work with Finance, Sales, Operations, and venue teams to understand their needs and turn them into models and metrics they trust. Own ingestion for your domains. Set up and maintain Fivetran connectors, land data in bronze, and handle schema drift and load failures. Model the business. Build dbt models that move data through bronze, silver, and gold, and shape gold around how CHG runs so people outside the data team can understand and use it. Own the semantic layer. Set metrics, dimensions, and relationships so a number means the same thing in a dashboard, a search, or an agent’s answer. Tune synonyms and descriptions so a model picks the right measure, trace wrong answers to the root cause, and help us decide where each definition lives. Power self-service in ThoughtSpot. Build the models and Liveboards that let teams explore data on their own, and turn the questions people actually ask into new test cases. Own the quality of conversational analytics. Test answers the way you’d test code. Build and maintain a golden question set of real business questions paired with certified answers as your test cases, run them as a regression suite on every model or semantic change, and block releases that fail. Back your models with dbt tests and clear documentation. Apply governance day to day. Tag sensitive data at ingestion, apply access controls such as tag-based masking and row access policies, and follow the standards the team sets, so an agent only returns what the person asking is allowed to see. Keep it fast and fresh. Monitor freshness, data quality, and pipeline health so problems surface to you before they reach a dashboard or an agent’s answer. Tune query and model performance, from incremental dbt models to warehouse sizing, so answers come back fast and Snowflake costs stay in check. Work AI-native. Lead with specs, then hand agents end-to-end tasks, from exploring source data to building models, tests, and documentation. Let agents run loose in the wild (with some guardrails in place). You hold agent and human work to the same review bar, so code from Claude and code from a teammate get the same scrutiny. Share what you learn, and help set the playbook for agentic data work. What We Look For: You have 3+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI development, building data products people rely on. You write strong SQL and have built and maintained dbt models in production. You’ve worked in a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. You’ve worked with ELT ingestion tools like Fivetran and can troubleshoot source-data issues such as schema changes, late-arriving data, and API limits. You understand data modeling: dimensional models, medallion layering, and clear reasoning about grain, slowly changing dimensions, and event lifecycles. You’ve built dashboards or self-service data products that people use to make decisions. You test and document your work as a habit. You’re curious about the business. You ask what decision a request supports before you start building. You use AI agents for real multi-step work, like writing SQL and dbt models, generating tests, and drafting documentation, and you verify what they produce. You explain your work clearly to technical and non-technical partners. You take ownership. You see work through, ask for help when you’re stuck, and look for ways to make things better. Bonus Points You’ve evaluated LLM or natural-language analytics output, for example with golden sets or regression testing. You’ve worked in hospitality, events, real estate, or another customer-centric, multi-location business. jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.jd:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews. 



Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.


The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.


Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures. 



The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people. 



We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.



This analyst turns Outset's own data into decisions faster than a traditional analytics hire would, by using AI tools as a core part of the workflow rather than bolting them on afterward. They're as comfortable writing a SQL query to understand critical business data accurately, as they are building a small internal tool, script, or AI skill that answers a recurring question without a human re-running it every week. 

The job is part analysis, part automation - someone who'd rather build the dashboard-that-builds-itself than ship the same report by hand twice. Improving processes and workflows across the company excites them and they love to build tools to help internal teams across the business move, manage and understand data.



Responsibilities

 - Answer recurring business questions across GTM, People, Product and Engineering using SQL, Python, and whatever AI tooling gets there fastest.

 - Build small internal tools - vibe coded apps, Slack bots, scripts, lightweight dashboards, AI skills - that eliminate a manual report or a repeated ad hoc request.

 - Partner with stakeholders to figure out what they actually need before building anything.

 - Maintain and improve data pipelines so the underlying numbers are trustworthy, not just the tools on top of them.

 - Evaluate new AI tools and workflows as they come out, and decide which are actually worth adopting internally vs. hype.

 - Document what you build well enough that someone else can run it without you in the room.

 - Flag data quality issues and inconsistent definitions before they turn into bad decisions.

Qualifications

 - 3+ years in a data analyst, analytics engineer, or BI role, with real SQL and Python fluency.

 - Hands-on experience using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, or similar) to build something real - a script, an agent, an automation - not just to summarize text.

 - A builder's instinct: when a manual process repeats twice, the next step is automating it, not doing it a third time.

 - Able to go from a vague stakeholder ask to a specific, well-scoped answer without heavy hand-holding.

 - Clear written communication - can explain a finding or a tool to someone non-technical in a few sentences.

 - Experience at a startup where the data stack and tooling were still being built, not inherited mature.

 - Exposure to building or prompting AI agents/workflows (not just using chat interfaces).

 - Familiarity with modern BI/data tools (dbt, Looker, Hex, or similar).

jobs.title: Market Analyst
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

jobs.jd: The Amazon Security Experiences (ASE) organization is the data intelligence backbone of Amazon Security. Working on well-defined problems with guidance from senior engineers, you will maintain data lineage understanding, apply analytics and visualization tools, and deliver reliable insights on schedule. jobs.title: Marketing Analyst - Network Optimization
jobs.jd:
ABOUT GEN:

Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.

At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.

If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen.




ROLE OVERVIEW

The Marketing Analyst – Network Optimization will use data and experimentation to uncover what drives marketplace performance, turning analysis into clear, actionable recommendations that shape the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of tests. This role sits at the intersection of marketing analytics, data science, product, and commercial strategy.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, moving quickly from questions to analysis to action. At the core of the role: translating business questions into testable hypotheses, designing sound experiments, monitoring live tests, and delivering clear, data-driven readouts that inform optimization decisions — supported by day-to-day management of the test agenda.



Key Responsibilities

Marketplace and Marketing Analytics

 - Conduct exploratory analysis to understand changes in customer behavior, traffic quality, offer engagement, and downstream outcomes.

 - Monitor marketplace and funnel performance to identify optimization opportunities across customer experience, offer display, partner performance, and monetization.

 - Support opportunity sizing and business-case development for proposed optimization initiatives.

 - Partner with analytics and data science teams to improve measurement quality, data reliability, and experimentation velocity.

 - Help develop repeatable processes for rapid testing, post-test analysis, and continuous optimization.

Test Design and Execution

 - Support the development and maintenance of a prioritized test-and-learn agenda across network optimization, offer display, ranking, curation, pricing, eligibility, and related marketplace levers.

 - Translate business opportunities and performance signals into clear hypotheses, test objectives, target populations, success metrics, and guardrail metrics.

 - Help design A/B, holdout, multivariate, and other controlled experiments in partnership with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and business stakeholders.

 - Coordinate test setup, launch readiness, audience splits, documentation, timelines, and stakeholder communication.

 - Track execution from initial idea through implementation, launch, monitoring, analysis, and final recommendation.

 - Work quickly and pragmatically while maintaining analytical rigor and attention to detail.

Test Readouts and Reporting

 - Monitor live experiments and summarize performance across key funnel and marketplace metrics.

 - Produce concise, decision-oriented test readouts covering methodology, results, limitations, learnings, and recommended next steps.

 - Analyze metrics such as impressions, click-through rate, conversion, click-to-funded rate, revenue, revenue per lead, revenue per click, and partner or network efficiency.

 - Identify meaningful changes, anomalies, and emerging opportunities that require investigation or follow-up testing.

jobs.title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
jobs.jd:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

 - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

 - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

 - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

 - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

 - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

 - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

 - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer 5 - Ads Identity & Signals
jobs.jd: At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next. In 2022 we launched a new lower-priced, ad-supported tier, and we are building an in-house, world-class ad-tech ecosystem to give our members more choice and to offer advertisers a premium, better-than-linear-TV experience. We are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix. The Identity & Signals team builds the identity foundation of the Netflix ads business — the graph and matching systems that let us recognize the same person or household across signals, devices, and partner data sources, and that determine which signals we can responsibly and accurately use for targeting, measurement, and reporting. We build and maintain the identity graph, run and evaluate entity-matching and resolution pipelines, and manage relationships with identity providers so that advertisers and internal teams can trust the signals underneath every campaign. This is a foundational role on a small, high-leverage team. You will build the analytics and data infrastructure that powers identity matching and graph construction — designing the tables, pipelines, and metrics that let the team and its stakeholders understand match quality, coverage, and drift over time. You'll work end-to-end: from raw signal ingestion, through matching logic and graph construction, to the dashboards and data products that make identity health visible and actionable across the company. In This Role, You Will Design, build, and maintain the data models and pipelines that support identity graph construction, entity matching, and identity resolution across first-party and third-party signals. Partner with data engineering and software engineering to productionize matching logic, ensuring pipelines are scalable, well-tested, and monitored for data quality and drift. Build metrics, dashboards, and analytics that quantify match rate, match quality, coverage, and graph stability, and that surface anomalies before they affect downstream campaigns. Work closely with data science to evaluate and improve matching algorithms, providing the clean, well-documented data and features needed to test and iterate on models. Manage and evaluate the analytics relationship with external identity providers (e.g., Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp), including onboarding new sources, validating match performance, and monitoring ongoing data quality. Translate identity graph and matching concepts — nodes, edges, match confidence, deterministic vs. probabilistic matching — into clear, actionable insights for product, sales, and other non-technical stakeholders. Collaborate with product and cross-functional partners to define identity requirements, evaluate trade-offs (accuracy vs. coverage vs. privacy), and prioritize roadmap work. Communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of the company. We Are Looking For 5+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, or similar role working with large-scale data. Experience working with graph data structures and graph-based data models (e.g., property graphs, graph databases, or graph analytics on top of relational/columnar stores). Familiarity with entity matching / identity resolution concepts — deterministic and probabilistic matching, fuzzy matching, blocking/candidate generation, and match quality evaluation. Knowledge of, or direct experience working with, identity providers such as Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp, or similar data/identity partners. Strong SQL and Python skills, with experience building and maintaining production data pipelines. Experience designing data models, metrics, and dashboards that make complex technical systems understandable to non-technical stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to collaborate closely across data engineering, software engineering, data science, and product teams. Ability to work independently, drive your own projects, and make compelling cases for prioritization. Embodies the Netflix values while bringing a new perspective to continue improving our culture. Nice To Have Experience with ad-tech identity concepts — cross-device identity, household graphs, cookie/ID deprecation, or media measurement. Experience with graph databases or graph-processing frameworks (e.g., Neo4j, Neptune, GraphFrames, or similar). Familiarity with our ML/data stack (Metaflow) or comparable large-scale data tooling. Experience working with privacy-sensitive data and an understanding of relevant data governance and privacy considerations for identity data. Experience applying GenAI to boost developer/analytics productivity. Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $330,000.00 - $566,000.00. This compensation range will vary based on location. Netflix provides comprehensive benefits including Health Plans, Mental Health support, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with employer match, Stock Option Program, Disability Programs, Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts, Family-forming benefits, and Life and Serious Injury Benefits. We also offer paid leave of absence programs. Full-time hourly employees accrue 35 days annually for paid time off to be used for vacation, holidays, and sick paid time off. Full-time salaried employees are immediately entitled to flexible time off. See more details about our Benefits here . Netflix is a unique culture and environment. Learn more here . Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner. We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, caste, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic makeup, marital status, or military service. Job is open for no less than 7 days and will be removed when the position is filled.
